q: Right-brain stroke in this recap. Which body side is weak?

opts.why: Motor nerves cross in the brainstem. Right brain controls the left body.
Right body weakness is a left-brain stroke.
This recap’s motor finding is one-sided, opposite the brain side.
The motor finding is the opposite body side, not the face alone.

q: Left-brain stroke in this recap often adds what?

opts.why: Left-brain strokes often bring speech problems (left frontal) plus right-body weakness.
Poor awareness of the deficit is the right-brain picture in this recap.
Left brain hits the right body, and often speech.
Right-body weakness is the laterality. Left-brain strokes often add speech on top of that.

q: Most strokes in this recap are which type?

opts.why: About 87 percent are ischemic clots. About 13 percent are hemorrhagic bleeds.
Hemorrhagic is about 13 percent. Ischemic is about 87 percent.
They are not even. Ischemic is about 87 percent.
Most are clots. You still wait for CT to treat the type.

q: Why does this recap wait on a head CT before treating stroke type?

opts.t: Clot care can kill the bleed
opts.why: Clot treatment breaks clots. Bleed treatment wants clotting. Treatment for one can kill the other. CT tells them apart.
You still get last known well. CT is to choose clot versus bleed care.
You do not treat the type. Definitive care waits on CT.
Do not give aspirin for stroke. CT sorts the type.

q: Stroke-like patient in this recap. What must you check before you lock in stroke?

opts.why: Hypoglycemia can perfectly mimic stroke. Always check glucose in altered or stroke-like patients before you commit to stroke.
The recap story is they almost flew a textbook-looking stroke before anyone checked sugar. Check sugar first.
Do not give aspirin for stroke. Check sugar.
Droop does not skip the sugar check. Hypoglycemia can look just like that.

q: Found down this morning, last seen normal at 1900 yesterday. Last known well in this recap?

opts.why: Last known well is the last time anyone saw them normal. If that was 1900 yesterday, last known well is 1900 yesterday.
Arrival time is not last known well. Use last seen normal.
Found-down time is not last seen normal. Use 1900 yesterday.
This recap’s example uses 1900 yesterday, not midnight.

q: Suspected stroke. Aspirin in this recap?

opts.t: Do not give it for stroke
opts.why: Do not give aspirin for stroke. Aspirin in this recap is for suspected cardiac chest pain.

q: Ischemic stroke clot-busters in this recap are often only given within about how long from onset?

opts.why: Thrombolytics are often only given if within about 3 hours from onset. Times vary by protocol.
Brain cells start dying in about 10 minutes. The common clot-buster window is about 3 hours.
This recap’s common window is about 3 hours, not 24.

opts.t: No time limit at all here

q: Which headache does this recap want you to worry about?

opts.why: Sudden-onset severe worst-ever headache is a red flag, and so is headache plus fever, seizure, altered mental status, or trauma.
Tension headaches are usually non-emergent, but you still cannot be sure in the field.
Sinus headaches are usually not 911 calls. Worst-ever sudden is the red flag.

opts.t: Mild ache after a long day
opts.why: A mild long-day ache is not the red-flag picture. Sudden worst-ever is.

q: Severe headache. Over-the-counter pills in this recap?

opts.why: Do not recommend OTC meds if they are not in your scope to give. Push hospital if they called 911.
Do not recommend ibuprofen or Tylenol from the field.

opts.t: Tell them to take Tylenol now
opts.why: You have no EMS headache medicine and you do not recommend OTC pills.

q: They understand you but cannot get words out. What does this recap call that?

opts.why: Expressive aphasia: they understand you but cannot get words out or make sense.
Receptive aphasia is not processing what you said, and they may talk nonsense.
Dysarthria is slurred or poorly articulated speech, not cannot-get-words-out aphasia.
Cannot get words out is new aphasia unless that is their old baseline.

q: Arms out, palms up, eyes closed in this recap. What are you looking for?

opts.why: Arm drift: one arm drifts down and suggests weakness on that side.
Equal lift is a negative drift. You are looking for one arm drifting down.
The smile is the face check. This stem is the arm-drift test.
